A0056.title: Vulnerability Remediation
A0056.definition: After identifying security vulnerabilities in a computer system, network, or application, taking a series of measures to patch or eliminate those vulnerabilities in order to reduce the risk of potential attackers exploiting them for unauthorized access, data leakage, destruction, or other malicious activities.
A0056.description: Key vulnerability remediation methods include: security patch application — security patches released by manufacturers or developers typically contain fixes for known vulnerabilities, and organizations should apply these patches promptly to ensure vulnerabilities are addressed; system configuration updates — updating system and application configurations to fix configuration errors that may cause vulnerabilities, such as disabling default passwords and restricting unnecessary services; code review and fixes — reviewing source code or binary code for application vulnerabilities, identifying potential security issues and fixing them; network security device configuration — updating and fixing configurations on network and security devices to address potential vulnerabilities; data encryption and access control — using data encryption and strengthened access controls to improve overall system security.
A0056.limitation: Fixes require development, compatibility testing, and deployment windows, leaving vulnerabilities exploitable during delays. Patches may introduce regressions, miss related flaws, or remain unavailable when a vendor ends support. Complex environments must balance downtime against business continuity, while incomplete asset inventories and fragmented versions can leave some systems unpatched.
